# The wasm regressions for secp256k1 (S8 part B4). `make check` builds
# test/wasm/secp.lang, gives the NAME ARGS part of each row to build/wasmtool
# and compares the output with the RESULT parts. A row is
# `NAME ARGS => RESULT`. `addX a b c d` and `addY a b c d` are the x and the
# y of `ecAdd (pair a b) (pair c d)`. `mulX x y k` and `mulY x y k` are the x
# and the y of `ecMul (pair x y) k`. G is (0x79be...1798, 0x483a...d4b8) and
# (0, 0) is the point at infinity. Each RESULT came one time from the stdout
# of `langc --kit eval test/wasm/secp.lang NAME ARGS`. The x and the y of 2G
# (rows 1 to 4) and of 3G (rows 5 to 8) are the same as the published values
# (0xc6047f94...9ee5, 0x1ae168fe...e52a) and (0xf9308a01...36f9,
# 0x388f7b0f...e672). A row with RESULT `trap` has a point that is not on the
# curve or a coordinate equal to p.
# `sigOk k r z m e` is `schnorrOk k r z m e` (S8 part B3): k is the x of the
# key, r is the x of R, z is the response, m is the head and e is the entry.
# The first sigOk row is a valid signature (the lift takes the smaller y, and
# c = H(H(H(H(tag, k), r), m), e) mod n). Each of the other 4 rows changes
# one word: z + 1, z = n, an r that is not the x of a point, and k = p. The
# RESULT of these 4 rows is 0, not trap.
